subject: VPC surface / backplane alignment — ops + control/data split
messages:
From: Colin Brooks <colin.brooks@evergreenhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@evergreenhealth.com>, infra-ops <infra-ops@evergreenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Alignment request — VPC surface vs backplane (control/data)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team dug in and we want to make sure we and Redwood are aligned on two things before we start the on-prem pilot:

1) "Surface" interfaces (tenant-facing ingress) vs the "backplane" (control plane / KVC cache and internal traffic). We need a crisp mapping of which ports/protocols and flows will egress the customer edge and which remain inside the colo network.
2) Evidence for our security team that control-plane traffic can be constrained and audited separately (logs, cert rotation, KMS handshake).

Could you share a reference diagram + runbook that shows the control/data split and proposed canary cutover steps? We'd like the diagram to reflect the east-west tenant proxy + north-south surface so our NOC can sign off.

Appreciate it —
Colin

--
Colin Brooks
Head of Cloud Architecture
Evergreen Health Systems
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Colin Brooks <colin.brooks@evergreenhealth.com>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@evergreenhealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alignment request — VPC surface vs backplane (control/data)

Hi Colin —

Thanks for the clear asks. I attached a compact reference diagram (vpc_surface_backplane_v2.pdf) and a short canary/runbook checklist we use for private deployments. High level notes:

- Surface (tenant ingress):
  - TLS termination at the edge proxy (mutual TLS optional depending on cert ownership)
  - Public-facing egress limited to health-check endpoints and metrics (no control-plane tokens)
  - Per-tenant routing table in the leaf router (annotated in the diagram)

- Backplane (control / KV cache / agent-to-control flows):
  - Only allowed over the dedicated internal fabric; uses mTLS with per-service certs issued by customer KMS (we support HSM integrations)
  - Strongly recommend pinning control-plane hosts to a private CIDR and a dedicated VLAN for observability and capture
  - KV cache replication and snapshot writes are on a separate path from tenant inference traffic (diagram shows out-of-band replication over BGP peering inside the colo)

- Auditability / evidence for compliance:
  - We capture request-level traces and export audit logs to a customer-managed SIEM via secure forwarder (see section 3 in diagram notes)
  - Cert rotation is surfaced as an operator-runbook step; we can integrate with your KMS to automate rotation if desired

I'll loop Mateo and Soojin for deeper network/ops annotations. If those two are OK with the topology, we can target a staged canary next week.

Attachments: vpc_surface_backplane_v2.pdf; canary-rollout-runbook.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Field Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-04T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alignment request — VPC surface vs backplane (control/data)

Kimberly / Mateo / Colin —

Looping in high-level build comments after reviewing the diagram and runbook. Inline notes below; quoting Colin for context:

> Our infra team dug in and we want to make sure we and Redwood are aligned on two things before we start the on-prem pilot:
>
> 1) "Surface" interfaces (tenant-facing ingress) vs the "backplane" (control plane / KVC cache and internal traffic). We need a crisp mapping of which ports/protocols and flows will egress the customer edge and which remain inside the colo network.

Responses / suggestions:
- Ports/protocols: we recommend keeping all control RPCs on TLS 9901 (example) and KV replication on 9910; inference surface traffic stays on 443/HTTP2. That gives a simple ACL set for NOC.
- Egress: surface may require outbound to monitoring SaaS (metrics.telemetry.redwood.com) — we can proxy and forward over a single egress IP to minimize firewall rules.

> 2) Evidence for our security team that control-plane traffic can be constrained and audited separately (logs, cert rotation, KMS handshake).

Responses / suggestions:
- Auditing: we will provide an audit bundle (signed) for the canary window containing: access logs, control-plane RPC traces, and KV snapshot manifests.
- KMS handshake: we support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed short-lived certs. For air-gapped scenarios we recommend customer KMS + occasional signed attestations from our control plane.

Operational concerns:
- MTU and jumbo frames: if you're using overlay networking, confirm tenant MTU so our KVchunking doesn't fragment (note in diagram).
- Observability: ensure a flow for exporting 1:1 control-plane traceroutes to your NOC.

If Colin/Sanjay are good with the port mappings and the single-egress-proxy approach, we'll update the diagram to include explicit ACL rule examples and a vendor-neutral iptables/nftables snippet for your team to apply.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Colin Brooks <colin.brooks@evergreenhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Alignment request — VPC surface vs backplane (control/data)

Colin / team —

Thanks everyone. Quick summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth before the pilot:

Decisions agreed:
- Control plane traffic will be isolated on private VLAN 120 / CIDR 10.120.0.0/22 and use mTLS on TCP 9901; KV replication will use 9910.
- Tenant surface traffic remains on 0.0.0.0:443 (HTTP/2), routed via the edge proxy with per-tenant SNI.
- We will deliver an audit bundle for the canary and keep logs in your SIEM via secure forwarder (encrypted channel).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Soojin: add explicit ACL examples and MTU notes to the diagram (updated PDF) — ETA 2026-09-10.
- Mateo: produce the signed-canary checklist and evidence template (canary-rollout-runbook.xlsx) — ETA 2026-09-09.
- Colin/Sanjay: confirm that Evergreen will expose a single egress IP for proxy forwarding and confirm KMS preference (customer-managed or Redwood-managed) — ETA 2026-09-09.

We will not start the canary until Evergreen signs the runbook and provides the egress IP + KMS preference. Once those are in, we schedule a short staging cutover (low-traffic tenant) and generate the first audit bundle.

If any NOC/security folks want to join a 30m call to walk the updated diagram, say when and we will set it up.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Field Deployments
Redwood Inference
